istanze.titolo: Minimum green-space thresholds for the city
istanze.descrizione: Mandatory minimum standards of public green space for each neighbourhood. Protection of green areas and an obligation to compensate for every new building.
istanze.obiettivo: A guaranteed minimum of public green space in every neighbourhood of Turin
istanze.obiettivoSpiega: The three tables each wrote one part. Together they became a citizens’ initiative proposal, delivered to the Consulta cittadina del Verde.

conclusa.norma: The Consulta’s rules require at least 1,500 signatures.
tappe: 2,140 signatures at stalls in the tables’ neighbourhoods.
The proposal has been filed with the Consulta.
Discussion and vote in the Consulta
Whoever submitted the proposal can present it at the session.

restituzione.posto: Parco Dora, the Red Benches lawn
restituzione.programma: tell people about the delivered proposal and what happens now. A shared snack, open to everyone.

tavoli.titolo: How much green, neighbourhood by neighbourhood
tavoli.domanda: How much green space the people living in a neighbourhood need, and how to count it.
tavoli.parte: Writes the minimum green-space threshold, neighbourhood by neighbourhood.
soggetti: Orti della Zappa Gentile di Mirafiori Sud
Assemblea del Cortile Grande delle Vallette
Gruppo Radici Basse di San Donato
tavoli.finale: In every neighbourhood, usable public green space within a ten-minute walk from home. The threshold starts from the 9 square metres per inhabitant that ministerial decree 1444 of 1968 requires for parks, play and sport, but it is counted neighbourhood by neighbourhood and only where people can go in. Where the threshold isn’t met, the neighbourhood gets priority for new green spaces. The count is redone and published every year.

incontri.avanti: The table is set: four neighbourhoods, one question about the green space people need.
incontri.parlato: Each group described the green space in its own neighbourhood: where it is, how far from home, what state it’s in. In Barriera and Vallette the green exists on paper, but it’s broken up into flowerbeds and traffic islands where no one can stay.
incontri.aperto: How to measure the green space people can really use, not just what exists on paper.
compiti: Gruppo Radici Basse di San Donato
looks for public data on green space by district
Tutti i soggetti
mark the truly usable green places on a map of their own neighbourhood

incontri.avanti: Decided what to count: only green space where people can go in, sit down and play.
incontri.parlato: Public data were compared with the hand-drawn maps. The data also count flowerbeds and roadside verges; the hand-drawn maps show that in some areas the usable green is less than half. It was decided to count only open, accessible green space.
incontri.aperto: What distance from home counts as close.
compiti: Orti della Zappa Gentile di Mirafiori Sud
proposes a walking distance to use as the measure
Comitato Ombre Lunghe di Barriera
tries the count across all of Barriera

incontri.avanti: A shared measure: usable green space within a ten-minute walk from home.
incontri.parlato: The Barriera count worked. It was decided to measure the green space reachable in ten minutes on foot, so the count works for people without a car, people pushing a pram and people who walk slowly.
incontri.aperto: What threshold to propose: too high and it’s never met, too low and nothing changes.
compiti: Tutti i soggetti
count the green space within ten minutes of three points in their own neighbourhood

incontri.avanti: Text ready: the minimum threshold and how it’s calculated.
incontri.avantiLungo: The table’s part is ready: in every neighbourhood, usable public green space within a ten-minute walk, with a minimum threshold per inhabitant. Where it’s missing, the neighbourhood gets priority for new green spaces.
incontri.parlato: The counts from the four neighbourhoods showed the gap between areas. The threshold is written as a guaranteed minimum per neighbourhood, not as a city average, because the average hides the neighbourhoods where green space is missing.
incontri.aperto: Nothing: the part is ready. The text goes to Table 3, to link it to compensation.
compiti: Assemblea del Cortile Grande delle Vallette
takes the text to Table 3

tavoli.domanda: How to make everyday streets walkable in summer.
tavoli.parte: Writes the obligation to provide shade along everyday streets.
soggetti: Ciclofficina La Catena Lenta di Borgo Vittoria
Anziani del circolo Le Panchine di Lucento
tavoli.finale: Along the routes to schools, markets and clinics, continuous shade from trees. Every tree planted gets guaranteed care for its first three years, water included.

incontri.avanti: The table is set: in summer some streets can no longer be walked.
incontri.parlato: Parents, older people and cyclists described the same routes: from home to school, to the market, to the community centre. In summer some go without a single tree for hundreds of metres.
incontri.aperto: Which streets to start with.
compiti: Genitori della Campanella di Aurora
mark the most used home–school routes
Anziani del circolo Le Panchine di Lucento
mark the routes to markets and clinics

incontri.avanti: Streets chosen: the routes to schools, markets and clinics.
incontri.parlato: Putting the routes together showed that they repeat: almost all of them pass schools, markets and clinics. It was decided that shade must be guaranteed there first.
incontri.aperto: Who looks after new trees in their first years, when they need water most.
compiti: Ciclofficina La Catena Lenta di Borgo Vittoria
collects how other cities look after young trees

incontri.avanti: First draft: continuous shade along everyday routes.
incontri.parlato: The first draft was read. It was added that every tree planted gets guaranteed care for its first three years: without water, many young trees don’t survive the next summer.
incontri.aperto: How to link shade to new buildings.
compiti: Ciclofficina La Catena Lenta di Borgo Vittoria
writes the text with the corrections
Tutti i soggetti
read the text before {mese:2026-05-15}

incontri.avanti: Text ready: shade along daily routes and trees looked after for three years.
incontri.parlato: The text was read aloud and approved. The part about new buildings goes to Table 3, which is writing the compensation rule.
incontri.aperto: Nothing: the part is ready.
compiti: Genitori della Campanella di Aurora
hand the text to the people putting the proposal together

tavoli.titolo: Every metre built, a metre given back
tavoli.domanda: What someone who builds on open land must give back to the neighbourhood.
tavoli.parte: Writes the obligation to compensate for every new building.
soggetti: Comitato del Binario Morto di Vanchiglia
Assemblea del Prato Lungo di Parco Dora
tavoli.finale: Whoever builds on open land gives back the same surface as usable public green space, in the same neighbourhood. If there’s no room, asphalt is removed: school yards, squares, car parks. It applies first of all in neighbourhoods below the threshold.

incontri.avanti: The table is set: every new building site takes away land.
incontri.parlato: Each group brought a case: a car park instead of a lawn, a building on a plot the neighbourhood used. It was decided to work on a simple rule: whoever builds gives back green space.
incontri.aperto: Give back the green where: on the same plot, in the same neighbourhood or elsewhere in the city?
compiti: Osservatorio Terra Nuda
gathers how much land has been built on in recent years

incontri.avanti: Decided: green space is given back in the same neighbourhood.
incontri.parlato: Giving back green space far away doesn’t help people who lose the lawn outside their door. It was decided that compensation stays in the neighbourhood, and that it applies first in the neighbourhoods below the threshold written by Table 1.
incontri.aperto: What happens if there’s no free space in the neighbourhood.
compiti: Assemblea del Prato Lungo di Parco Dora
tests the rule on three recent building sites

incontri.avanti: Text ready: every metre built goes back to green in the same neighbourhood.
incontri.avantiLungo: The part is ready. Whoever builds on open land gives back the same surface as usable public green space, in the same neighbourhood. If there’s no room, asphalt is removed. With this part the proposal is finished and moves on to the signature collection.
incontri.parlato: The test on three building sites showed that space can almost always be found by removing asphalt. The text was approved and joined to the other two parts.
incontri.aperto: Nothing: the proposal moves on to the signature collection.
compiti: Tutti i soggetti
collect signatures in their own neighbourhood

istanze.descrizione: Regulatory tools against the replacement of neighbourhood communities: protection for long-standing tenants, limits on speculative increases.
istanze.obiettivo: Municipal tools so that people who live in a neighbourhood can stay when it changes
istanze.obiettivoSpiega: All the tables work towards this goal. Two parts are ready; when the third is ready too, the proposal goes to the municipalities of the tables’ cities.

tavoli.domanda: Which signs show that a neighbourhood is losing its residents.
tavoli.parte: Writes how to measure, year by year, the replacement of residents.
soggetti: Comitato dei Portici Nuovi della Bolognina
tavoli.finale: A public observatory, run jointly by the municipality and residents, publishes four indicators per neighbourhood every year: families leaving, evictions, shops closing, rents. Above a threshold, the neighbourhood becomes an area to protect and the other tables’ parts apply.

incontri.avanti: The table is set: four neighbourhoods changing fast.
incontri.parlato: Each group described the signs of change: rising rents, shops closing, neighbours leaving without anyone noticing. But nobody can say how many have really left.
incontri.aperto: Which numbers show that a neighbourhood is emptying of its residents.
compiti: Osservatorio dei Lampioni del Pigneto
gathers what public data exist on changes of residence

incontri.avanti: Four indicators chosen, to be counted every year.
incontri.parlato: Four indicators were chosen: how many families leave the neighbourhood, how many evictions, how many shops close, how much rents rise. Together they say more than each one alone.
incontri.aperto: Where to find eviction data neighbourhood by neighbourhood.
compiti: Comitato dei Portici Nuovi della Bolognina
asks its own municipality for the data
Rete dei Citofoni di NoLo
tests the four indicators on NoLo

incontri.avanti: First draft: a public observatory, with open data every year.
incontri.parlato: The NoLo test worked with three indicators out of four: eviction data by neighbourhood aren’t public. The draft asks the municipality to publish them, without names.
incontri.aperto: Who runs the observatory: the municipality alone, or together with residents.
compiti: Assemblea del Ballatoio di Aurora
writes the text with the jointly run observatory

incontri.avanti: Text ready: an observatory run jointly by the municipality and residents.
incontri.avantiLungo: The part is ready. Every year the observatory publishes the four indicators per neighbourhood, and the municipality and residents run it together. When the indicators pass a threshold, the neighbourhood becomes an area to protect.
incontri.parlato: The text was approved. It was decided that the exact threshold will be set together with the other tables, because it’s what triggers their protections.
incontri.aperto: The threshold: to be set with Table 2.
compiti: Osservatorio dei Lampioni del Pigneto
prepares three threshold options for the Turin meeting

prossimo.posto: Hosted by Assemblea del Ballatoio di Aurora
prossimo.programma: set, with the people coming from Table 2, the threshold above which a neighbourhood becomes an area to protect.

tavoli.domanda: What a neighbourhood loses when its local shops close, and how to keep them.
tavoli.parte: Writes the protections for local shops and ground-floor premises.
soggetti: Botteghe del Piano Terra di Porta Palazzo

incontri.avanti: The table is set: when a shop closes, the neighbourhood loses a point of reference.
incontri.parlato: The talk was about what a neighbourhood loses when a shop stays empty or becomes a place for tourists: somewhere to leave your keys, to ask, where older people pass every day.
incontri.aperto: How to tell a neighbourhood shop from any other shop.
compiti: Botteghe del Piano Terra di Porta Palazzo
gathers how other cities identify the shops to protect

incontri.avanti: Decided what to protect: not the historic shop window, but the service to the neighbourhood.
incontri.parlato: Many cities protect historic shops for their age or their fittings. The table chose another criterion: what counts is the service the shop gives to the people living nearby, even if it opened recently.
incontri.aperto: What tools a municipality has to keep the rent of a ground floor low.
compiti: Comitato dei Ponti dell’Isola
gathers the tools municipalities already use

incontri.avanti: First draft: the municipality’s ground floors at reduced rent for neighbourhood shops.
incontri.parlato: The starting point was what the municipality can do right away: the ground-floor premises it owns. The draft reserves them for neighbourhood shops at reduced rent, and asks that they not be sold in the areas to protect.
incontri.aperto: What to do about private ground floors, which are the majority.
compiti: Assemblea dei Gradini della Sanità
writes the second version
Tutti i soggetti
count the empty ground floors on one street in their own neighbourhood

incontri.avanti: Empty ground floors counted: the draft extends to private premises empty for years.
incontri.parlato: Every street counted has ground floors that have been empty for years. The draft adds an incentive for private owners: whoever rents to a neighbourhood shop in an area to protect pays lower municipal taxes.
incontri.aperto: Whether the discount is sustainable for municipal budgets.
compiti: Comitato dei Ponti dell’Isola
asks someone who knows municipal budgets for an opinion

prossimo.programma: read the opinion on the budgets and finish the text of the part.

tavoli.titolo: Homes for the people who live in them
tavoli.domanda: What happens to public housing in neighbourhoods that are changing.
tavoli.parte: Writes how to keep the neighbourhood’s public housing for the people who live there.
soggetti: Comitato delle Scale B e C di Falchera
tavoli.finale: In the areas to protect, empty public flats become habitable again within set times, with a public list of those waiting. Whoever leaves home for the works has the right to return to the same neighbourhood.
tavoli.attesa: The table will meet again when Table 2 has finished too, to deliver the proposal together.

incontri.avanti: The table is set: in changing neighbourhoods, public housing is the last dam.
incontri.parlato: Each group described what happens to public housing in changing neighbourhoods: empty flats waiting years for works, sales, residents moved far away during renovations.
incontri.aperto: What a municipality can decide about public housing, and what it can’t.
compiti: Sportello La Soglia della Bolognina
works out who decides what, between municipality and region

incontri.avanti: Clear who decides: the table writes only what is up to the municipalities.
incontri.parlato: Many rules on public housing are made by the regions. The table chose to write only what a municipality can do: deadlines for repairing empty flats, and the right to return to the same neighbourhood after the works.
incontri.aperto: How many months is a fair time to repair an empty flat.
compiti: Assemblea delle Cento Finestre dell’Esquilino
writes the first draft

incontri.avanti: Text ready: empty flats repaired within set times, and the right to return.
incontri.parlato: The draft was corrected and approved. The time to repair an empty flat is written as a commitment of the municipality, with a public list of the flats waiting.
incontri.aperto: Nothing: the part is ready.
compiti: Comitato delle Scale B e C di Falchera
keeps in touch with the other two tables

istanze.descrizione: An internal, permanent proposal: keeping Nomeprova itself open to discussion. Who gets left out? Who can’t manage to use it? What care practices are needed?
istanze.obiettivo: An app that no one has to leave out, and that no one has to depend on
istanze.obiettivoSpiega: It’s a permanent proposal: it never closes. Each table writes a rule for the app; when it’s ready it becomes part of Nomeprova, and the table starts again from what’s missing.

tavoli.domanda: Who can’t manage to use Nomeprova, and what stops them.
tavoli.parte: Writes the accessibility rules every new feature must follow.
tavoli.finale: Every new feature is tried first with at least three people who would find it hard to use. Large text, strong contrast, big buttons and plain words aren’t options: they’re the basics.

incontri.avanti: The table is set: who can’t manage to use Nomeprova?
incontri.parlato: Everyone brought the people they know who get left out: people who don’t see well, who don’t hear, who struggle to read Italian, who have an old phone. It was decided to try the app together with them, not to imagine them.
incontri.aperto: How to run the tests without turning them into an exam for the people taking part.
compiti: Scambio di Generazioni
organises two afternoons of testing with people who attend the project

incontri.avanti: Two afternoons of testing: eleven things that don’t work for everyone.
incontri.parlato: The tests brought up eleven difficulties: text too small, colours that get confused, buttons too close together, difficult words. Some can be fixed right away; others mean changing the way new features are designed.
incontri.aperto: Who checks that new features don’t repeat the same mistakes.
compiti: Associazione Parole Piane
rewrites the difficult words in easy-to-read language
Sportello Clic Lento di Barriera
writes the checklist

incontri.avanti: Text ready: no feature goes out without being tried by the people who risk being left out.
incontri.avantiLungo: The part is ready and the Nomeprova team has adopted it as an app rule: every new feature is tried first with people who would find it hard to use.
incontri.parlato: The checklist was read and approved. The Nomeprova team was there and adopted it. The table carries on: the first feature to go through the rule is the new map.
incontri.aperto: How to recognise the time of the people who do the tests.
compiti: Scambio di Generazioni
proposes a fixed testing schedule

prossimo.programma: try out the new map together: it’s the first feature to go through the rule.

tavoli.domanda: How to stop a civic app from becoming a habit that drains people.
tavoli.parte: Writes the rules so that Nomeprova doesn’t create dependence.

incontri.avanti: The table is set: can a civic app create dependence?
incontri.parlato: The talk was about how apps keep people glued to the screen: notifications, counters, rankings, endless scrolling. Nomeprova has already removed many of them; the table wants this to become a written rule, not a choice that can change.
incontri.aperto: What counts as a dependence mechanism, and what doesn’t.
compiti: Studenti dell’Ascolto
gather studies on the mechanisms that create habits

incontri.avanti: First draft: no counters, no rankings, no notifications you didn’t ask for.
incontri.parlato: The draft lists what Nomeprova will never do: count likes or people, make rankings, send notifications you didn’t ask for, scroll endlessly. There was a discussion about whether even the calendar could become a habit.
incontri.aperto: How to tell whether people use the app less than before, without tracking them.
compiti: Collettivo Ore Vuote
writes the second version

prossimo.posto: Hosted by Educatori del Marciapiede di Aurora
prossimo.programma: read the second version and decide what to do about the calendar.

istanze.descrizione: Legal protection for social centres and independent cultural spaces. A simplified procedure for institutional recognition.
istanze.obiettivo: A simple way to recognise self-managed spaces as the city’s commons
istanze.obiettivoSpiega: All the tables work towards this goal. The proposal asks for a shorter route for people who already look after a space.

tavoli.titolo: What makes a space a commons
tavoli.domanda: What very different self-managed spaces have in common.
tavoli.parte: Writes the criteria for recognising a self-managed space as a commons.
soggetti: Spazio Popolare La Ruggine di Borgo San Paolo

incontri.avanti: The table is set: four spaces, the same fear of closing.
incontri.parlato: Each space described what it does every week: after-school help, community gyms, rehearsal rooms, help desks. And how it lives with uncertainty: an expired contract, an announced eviction, a call for funding that never comes.
incontri.aperto: What such different spaces have in common.
compiti: Rete delle Porte Aperte
prepares a form for describing a space

incontri.avanti: A shared form for describing what a space does for the neighbourhood.
incontri.parlato: The form was approved: who uses it, how many days it’s open, what it offers without payment, who decides and how. In Naples people saw how civic use works in spaces the city has already recognised.
incontri.aperto: How many spaces to describe for the proposal to be credible.
compiti: Tutti i soggetti
describe at least five spaces in their own city with the form

incontri.avanti: Twenty spaces described: three things they all do.
incontri.parlato: The first twenty forms showed three things in common: doors open to anyone, free or pay-what-you-can activities, decisions taken in assembly. The table thinks these are what make a space a commons.
incontri.aperto: Whether years of activity are also needed, or the three things are enough.
compiti: Spazio Popolare La Ruggine di Borgo San Paolo
finishes the Turin forms
Laboratorio La Chiusa del Navile
finishes the Bologna ones

prossimo.posto: Hosted by Spazio Popolare La Ruggine di Borgo San Paolo
prossimo.programma: bring together the forms from the three cities and write the criteria.

tavoli.domanda: Which minimum rules make a space open and accountable to the city.
tavoli.parte: Writes the minimum rules every self-governance declaration must contain.
soggetti: Sala Prove Il Metronomo di Aurora
Palestra Popolare Il Sacco del Corvetto

incontri.avanti: The table is set: who decides in a space, and how.
incontri.parlato: Each space described how it makes decisions: weekly assemblies, rotas, who holds the keys. The proposal asks whoever runs a space to write a self-governance declaration: the table wants to understand what must go in it.
incontri.aperto: Whether a single model can work for such different spaces.
compiti: Assemblea dello Spazio La Bilancia
brings the rules the Naples space has given itself

incontri.avanti: Question written: not a single model, but minimum rules for everyone.
incontri.parlato: It was decided not to write a single model, but the minimum rules every declaration must contain: open doors, an assembly, public accounts, care of the place. Each space decides the rest.
incontri.aperto: How to ask for public accounts without putting people who collect pay-what-you-can donations in difficulty.
compiti: Palestra Popolare Il Sacco del Corvetto
writes the first list of minimum rules

prossimo.programma: read the list of minimum rules and correct it together.

tavoli.domanda: How to make a space safe without safety becoming the reason to close it.
tavoli.parte: Writes proportionate safety requirements for spaces that look after themselves.
tavoli.cerca: a safety technician willing to sit at the table.

prossimo.programma: introduce themselves and write the table’s question.

istanze.descrizione: A proposal to protect the right to housing: rent caps, action against speculative evictions, affordable public housing.
istanze.obiettivo: New urban rules on rent regulation
istanze.obiettivoSpiega: All the tables work towards this goal. Each writes one part; together they become a proposal to take to the municipalities.

tavoli.domanda: How to set a ceiling on rents, area by area.
tavoli.parte: Writes the rule for the rent ceiling by area.

incontri.avanti: The table is set: four groups, one shared question.
incontri.parlato: Each group described what renting costs today in its own neighbourhood and how much it has changed in a few years. In all four cities rents are rising faster than incomes, but no one has comparable figures.
incontri.aperto: Where to get real rents, since listings don’t say what people actually pay.
compiti: Tutti i soggetti
bring to Bologna the sources on rents they know in their own city

incontri.avanti: Chose where to start: the rents people really pay, not the ones in listings.
incontri.parlato: The possible sources were compared: listings, registered contracts, tenants’ accounts. Listings inflate prices and don’t say what is paid after negotiation; registered contracts can’t be consulted. It was decided to collect rents directly from tenants, with their consent.
incontri.aperto: How to collect rents without keeping personal data.
compiti: Rete Chiavi Sospese
prepares an anonymous form for collecting rents
Sportello Il Mattone del Pigneto
asks for an opinion on how to handle the data collected

incontri.avanti: A shared method for collecting real rents, neighbourhood by neighbourhood.
incontri.parlato: The anonymous form prepared in Bologna was approved. Every rent is noted the same way: area, square metres, year of the contract, monthly rent. No names, no exact address.
incontri.aperto: How many rents are needed in each area for the comparison to be serious.
compiti: Tutti i soggetti

app.programma: Each young person teaches an older person to make a video call. In return the older person teaches something they can do: a card game, a recipe, a knot.

mano.grande: Do you have a grandparent to bring along? That’s the biggest help.
